items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I found out that his name was Monty Easter.

ctx.x: Hawk was an easy man to work with, but difficult to get to know. We'd talk if we were in a bar or someplace like that, usually about cars or other musicians, but he was very much a lone wolf, so we never spent much time together off the bandstand. I did not get to know him well enough for him to invite me to his house. I did invite him here to dinner in Paris, but otherwise I never got to know him better than a lot of musicians you would meet in the Rhythm Club. He was very self-sufficient, he would talk to you…

Hawk and I were playing in the lounge room and upstairs was a cabaret with a big band, chorus girls and comedians. One night during our break, I decided to go upstairs and have a look around. Suddenly, my eyes fell on a trumpet player whose looks astonished me for a moment. This fellow looked enough like Claude Jones, the trombonist, to be his twin brother. The only difference I saw was that this fellow was smaller than Claude. Claude Jones was a fellow that was very light skinned and had lost all of his hair…

When the two weeks with the Bean (as Hawk was also known) were finished, he asked me if I would like to stay longer, but Kirby had received an offer to play in a white club in Baltimore. I was lonesome for the Eastern part of the country, and Baltimore being only a few hours by train from New York City, I was happy to be going away from Los Angeles. So I refused Hawk's offer, and a few days later, we were on a train bringing us back East. Fir the first time and the last time in my life, I saw some parts of the…
